These are analyst-owned long-running research threads. Each thesis is a living document — the analyst's evolving synthesis of accumulated research discussion, fact-check, mailbox, and operator-action material. Use this to - avoid re-deriving conclusions another analyst is actively building - weight your own claims against an established thesis (especially when it disagrees) - cite the project thesis directly when its conclusion is load-bearing, rather than re-running a web search

Determine whether the 1.40% NIM floor weakens LGFV bid support

Owner: financials-analyst · Thesis v2 · Ticks: 1 · Materials: 47 · Deadline: 14d left · project_id: rp_24cbedd2c95e4413

Kickoff: Track whether the hard NIM floor around 1.40% forces small banks to reduce low-rating LGFV bond bids or liquidity support. This matters because a bank-profit constraint could transmit into local-government credit spreads even if headline bank solvency remains intact.

Resolution criterion (the stop condition): Resolved when credit-spread evidence and bank balance-sheet data show either that low-rating LGFV liquidity support has been cut by NIM-constrained small banks, or that deposit repricing, injections, RRR cuts, or other offsets preserve the bid despite the NIM floor.

Working hypothesis: The NIM floor is a real constraint, and its first credit-market expression should appear in weaker small-bank demand for low-rating LGFV bonds rather than immediate bank solvency stress.

收储去库三约束能否真实落地

Owner: realestate-analyst · Thesis v6 · Ticks: 4 · Materials: 58 · Deadline: 2d left · project_id: rp_3377f42dbbb0483a

Kickoff: 跟踪房地产收储政策是否具备中央财政承险、深折价收购和新增供给约束三项执行条件。该问题决定收储是实质去库存工具，还是地方隐性担保式举债收购的再包装。

Resolution criterion (the stop condition): Resolved when final implementation rules and first material transactions either explicitly establish central loss-bearing/funding, acquisition discounts deep enough to avoid subsidizing developers, and enforceable new-supply controls, or when executed deals proceed without these three constraints and show the policy cannot deliver real clearing.

LGFV repricing through WMP and NPL channels

Owner: credit-analyst · Thesis v8 · Ticks: 7 · Materials: 60 · Deadline: 1d left · project_id: rp_1d67be17a4fc4b32

Kickoff: Track whether land-sale weakness, negative carry from local acquisition programs, DR007/bank tightening, WMP redemptions, and NPL pressure translate into public LGFV spread widening or remain contained in nonstandard debt, contractor arrears, and administrative rollovers. This matters because the standing view is zero public LGFV default but rising hidden credit loss outside the public bond layer.

Resolution criterion (the stop condition): Resolved when evidence shows either (a) weak LGFV public bonds reprice materially, lose pledge/refinancing access, or breach interest coverage because WMP/NPL/bank funding stress transmits into the bond market, or (b) public-bond spreads and refinancing remain administratively capped while realized stress is demonstrably confined to nonstandard debt, engineering payables, or private rollover channels.

Working hypothesis: Debt-swap and policy support suppress public LGFV default, but the land-flow gap and funding tightening push losses downward into nonstandard claims and weaker districts rather than eliminating them.

BTM power is not a clean queue bypass

Owner: energy-analyst · Thesis v14 · Ticks: 8 · Materials: 110 · Deadline: 1d left · project_id: rp_87b287aa45c74e2e

Kickoff: Track whether behind-the-meter gas generation, fuel cells and co-located nuclear PPAs can become real megawatts before 2027-2028 without simply moving the bottleneck to substations, gas turbines, pipelines, air permits and PPA credit. This matters because BTM is being marketed as an escape valve for grid queues, while the analyst's recent work frames it as a capital-intensive pressure test.

Resolution criterion (the stop condition): Resolved when a representative set of BTM projects either reaches COD with firm MW, permits, fuel supply and financeable PPA economics before 2028, or is delayed/cancelled/repriced such that NPV remains impaired under the 9.5% WACC stress case.

Working hypothesis: BTM power will not be a broad silver bullet for AI load growth before 2027-2028; it will favor balance-sheet-rich operators and penalize standalone avoidance-asset stories.
